meta.source: Native terminal and plugin profile-scope contracts; stable diagnostic pattern IDs
meta.selection: Retained local runtime and outgoing plugin hazards; retired platform/service/UI rules are removed

class_legend.C1: secret/home read outside the turn scope
class_legend.C3: side-worker / secondary entrypoint binds home only
class_legend.C4: per-profile key introduced, consumer reads raw name/id
class_legend.C5: adapter setting precedence & raw os.getenv fallback
class_legend.C8: config key registry vs runtime reader
class_legend.C10: profile lifecycle operations under live native owners

meta.usage: scripts/check_profile_scope_patterns.py --base origin/main [--head HEAD] | --files <paths>; optional path_regex restricts a pattern to matching repo-relative paths

patterns.scope_hint: Child builders bind the owning home, secrets, terminal policy and revocable session authority. Assert the actual HERMES_HOME and allowed credential set inside a real child.
patterns.why: An unbound MCP or delegated child inherits the launch profile instead of the conversation that owns it.

patterns.scope_hint: Optional memory plugins resolve credentials through the bound secret scope, not the ambient launch environment.
patterns.why: A profile omitting a credential must not silently borrow the launch profile account.

patterns.scope_hint: Launch-profile branches that treat 'no override' as 'no scope needed'; reserved-name checks.
patterns.why: The launch profile has its own contract (env-only TERMINAL_ENV=ssh, root files writable, a profile literally named 'main'); tests only asserted secondary isolation and the launch turn collapsed to file-only policy / the default namespace.

patterns.scope_hint: Module-level dicts keyed by session_id / task_id / server_name / display alone. Key must include hermes_home_key() or (scope, name) when a profile override is active; release must use the same key.
patterns.why: Two profiles legitimately share session names, DISPLAY numbers and MCP server names; the first profile's entry wins and B's release stops A's driver. #108935 keyed 36 caches and still missed browser_exec/computer_use.

patterns.scope_hint: MCP connection sharing across profiles: identity must include every credential source, including ones stored outside the config dict (OAuth token files under <profile>/mcp-tokens, client_cert/client_key).
patterns.why: Identical-looking MCP configurations can authenticate different accounts through profile-owned OAuth token files.

patterns.scope_hint: An effective config exposes the exact key consumed at runtime; every new setting needs a real reader and documented native CLI behavior.
patterns.why: A setting and its reader drifting to different names leaves a valid-looking configuration with no effect.

patterns.scope_hint: Profile clone materializes source symlinks before writes, publishes staging atomically, and rename/delete refuses live native owners under the maintenance fence.
patterns.why: A preserved source symlink can rewrite another profile; publishing a partial clone or renaming a live owner corrupts independent state.

patterns.scope_hint: Every secondary entrypoint must enter _session_profile_runtime_scope (home -> secrets -> terminal, same composition as a prompt turn) and hold its own registry reference on the DB.
patterns.why: Side workers bound HERMES_HOME only: they picked the launch terminal backend (local instead of the secondary's docker) and shared the parent's state.db handle so parent close() closed it under a running background turn.

patterns.scope_hint: command.dispatch's whole stage loop (quick -> plugin -> bundle -> skill) and slash.exec bundle routing must run under the session's profile home; use the home-keyed get_skill_commands().
patterns.why: The router bound the profile and said 'skill exists', the dispatcher scanned the launch home and answered 4018 'not a skill command' for every secondary-only skill.

patterns.scope_hint: Native profile RPCs that expand secret references, create MCP clients or spawn terminals bind the full session profile runtime scope, not home alone.
patterns.why: Binding only a home leaves credentials and terminal execution attached to the launch profile.

patterns.scope_hint: Post-turn file uploads, browser artifacts and connector callbacks bind the owning profile and selected terminal before resolving container mount paths.
patterns.why: A late callback resolving Docker mounts in the launch profile can drop the correct file or expose a same-named sibling artifact.

patterns.scope_hint: tools/registry.py: classify UnscopedSecretError from current_secret_scope() at the catch site, never from a branch hint; boot-time probes with no scope are DEBUG, not WARNING+traceback.
patterns.why: A boot-time reachability probe has no conversation scope; that absence is diagnostic, not evidence that another profile credential should be used.

patterns.scope_hint: Mark a home hydrated only when every source succeeded; each attempt replaces the prior snapshot; revoke stale snapshots.
patterns.why: Caching a failed credential-source hydration pins an empty or stale snapshot for every subsequent turn.

patterns.scope_hint: Import-time environment constants freeze launch-profile settings. Resolve effective config inside the owning scope or key caches by the native home identity.
patterns.why: An import-time value cannot follow an independent local profile, background turn or scoped configuration change.
